newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to discuss tea-for-oil deal with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to discuss tea-for-oil deal with Iraq.

text.p: The Sri Lanka Tea Board said on Monday it would be part of a delegation visiting the Iraqi capital Baghdad at the end of July or early August to discuss a tea-for-oil deal.

Tea Board chairman Clifford Ratwatte told Reuters the deal could involve around 6,000 tonnes of tea and was likely to start in 1998. He declined to give an estimate of the amount of oil that might be involved in the deal.

Ratwatte said the deal was likely to be similar to a tea-for-oil deal India recently negotiated with Iraq and would come under an arrangement supervised by the United Nations allowing limited oil sales in return for food.
"It is difficult to say the amounts involved, but we could sell 6,000 tonnes to Iraq," he said in an interview.
Ratwatte said he was confident a deal could be struck.
"In 1998, definitely they will buy our tea," he added.

The Sri Lankan negotiating team would be led by officials of the ministry of trade and include a representative of Sri Lanka's state oil company, Ceylon Petroleum Corp, and Sri Lanka's ministry of plantations.
Ratwatte said he would also be part of the delegation.
India's Tea Board said last week it had secured an order for 1,000 tonnes of tea, which the country was expected to export in the "immediate future".
Sri Lankan tea auction prices vary from 94 rupees ($1.60) to around 115 rupees per kg, depending on quality.
